items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: You know there’s Monty Alexander, there are a few musicians who make a living just traveling.

ctx.x: And all the musicians, it seems like all the jazz musicians, either by choice or necessity, have their educational part of what they do, because that’s where the money is.

And for many it’s the main thing. For instance a terrific pianist named Harold Danko, who is a full time professor at Eastman jazz, I took over his course at Manhattan School, this one course. The main part of his career is teaching now, because that’s security. There comes a point when, if you’re not a traveling musician now, and part of a permanent group, you either have to be a marketed star, made a star by the marketing mostly, and all that goes with that a manager and a record contract and the publicity and…
And as you said what is the product they’re turning out?
